title: Signed telemetry envelopes for on-prem & VPC collectors (chain-of-custody)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Overview: Implement a lightweight, backwards-compatible 'signed envelope' scheme for telemetry emitted by VPC and air-gapped on-prem collectors to provide a verifiable chain-of-custody between collector -> perimeter relay -> control-plane ingest. This reduces risk from compromised collectors, supports audit requirements for Private deployments, and enables per-tenant cryptographic provenance for traces/metrics/logs.

Background: Customers running Private/Dedicated often require stronger guarantees that telemetry originated from an authorized collector and was not replayed or tampered with during intermittent relay windows (air-gapped relays, manual handoff). Current pipelines assume network isolation + auth, but auditors ask for immutable provenance and ability to validate payload origin after-the-fact.

Proposal: Add a small envelope header (base64 JSON metadata + signature) attached to each telemetry batch. The header contains: collector_id, epoch timestamp, sequence number (per-collector), batch_hmac (over payload), optionally a short certificate chain id. Collectors sign envelopes with a device key provisioned via customer KMS/HSM or Redwood-issued short-term certificate for hosted private control planes. Relays verify signatures where possible and pass envelope metadata into ingest; control plane performs final verification and rejects invalid provenance when configured in tenant policy.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Full payload signing (RSA/ECDSA) vs HMAC + asymmetric envelope: we chose HMAC for batch payloads (low CPU overhead) combined with asymmetric signatures over the envelope metadata to avoid heavyweight per-token public-key ops on embedded/edge collectors.
- Backwards compatibility: envelopes are optional; control plane has a 'provenance_required' tenant flag. This allows gradual rollout without breaking older collectors.
- Payload size and latency: envelope adds ~200-400 bytes per batch; we will batch telemetry by default to amortize overhead and expose batching knobs in config.

Implementation plan:
1) Collector-side: implement EnvelopeBuilder in agent (Go) that attaches header and computes batch_hmac, uses local key material from /var/lib/redwood/collector-keys or KMS agent. Feature gate: --enable-signed-envelopes.
2) Relay-side: lightweight verification layer that optionally validates signature/sequence and adds X-Redwood-Provenance headers to HTTP/gRPC forward. Fail-open vs fail-closed controlled by tenant policy.
3) Control plane: verification service that re-checks signatures, stores provenance metadata alongside trace/metric logs, surfaces tampering alerts to Console and audit logs.
4) Console: new dashboard tiles to show provenance failures, per-collector sequence gaps, and signed vs unsigned ingestion rates.

Rollout and migration: start with internal staging tenants, then opt-in beta customers, then default "provenance_optional" for all Private deployments. For legacy collectors that cannot sign, provide a migration helper and a temporary gateway signing proxy.

Testing & validation: unit tests for envelope format, integration tests with offline relay simulation (air-gapped handoff), load test to measure CPU/latency impact on collectors (target <5% CPU change for standard 4-core collector), fuzz tests for replay/sequence attacks.

Documentation & compliance: Confluence spec link, operator runbook for provisioning collector keys, KMS integration guide, and audit checklist for SOC/ISO audits.
acceptance_criteria: Collector can emit signed envelopes with configurable batch size and key source
Relay and control-plane verify signatures and sequence numbers; invalid envelopes flagged
Console surfaces provenance metrics: signed vs unsigned rate, sequence gap alerts, per-collector tamper incidents
Load tests show <5% median CPU increase at typical batching config; latency impact measured and documented
Migration path documented and gateway signing proxy available for legacy collectors
Security review approved and KMS/HSM key provisioning flow documented
comments: 2025-02-14 - Spike: validated HMAC+asymmetric-envelopes approach in lab. Proof-of-concept attached (collector-agent branch).
2025-02-18 - Design review with Security: agreed on avoiding per-record signatures; recommended rotating short-term certs and including replay window checks.

2025-02-22 - Prototype: collector implementation (branch: feat/envelopes) generates envelopes and verifies locally; discovered edge-case with gzip-compressed batches — patched to compute HMAC over compressed bytes.
2025-02-26 - Ops: ran integration against onprem relay simulator with intermittent connectivity; sequence recovery logic added to relay and control-plane pairing.
2025-03-04 - QA: initial end-to-end tests passed for staging tenant; filing follow-ups for console UX and dashboard thresholds.
notes: Edge-case: some customers use custom relays that mutate headers; envelope metadata must be carried in-body if headers are unreliable.
Consider exposing an SDK for partner relays to validate and forward envelope metadata to reduce operational surprises.
We should coordinate with Dedicated capacity team to ensure keys are provisioned during Dedicated onboarding flow.
